text: A rider just flew out of a seventy mile an hour roller coaster. Here's how a lap bar is supposed to keep you in.
On October twelfth forty-two year old Hassan Kariem rode Goliath at Six Flags Over Georgia for his niece's birthday.
The ride climbs about two hundred feet and drops at up to seventy miles an hour.
Police say he was thrown from his seat and hit other riders before he fell beneath the ride. Four kids were hurt and he did not survive.
So how does a coaster keep you in your seat?
Over the big hills the train drops away faster than you fall so your body floats up off the seat.
Riders call that airtime. For a split second nothing is pushing you down.
The only thing holding you in is a padded lap bar locked down over your thighs.
Before the train leaves a light shows that every bar is locked and workers check each one by hand.
Investigators are looking at whether a part failed or a check was missed or both.
No cause has been found yet and the ride is still closed.
Six Flags shut down nine similar coasters and is adding seat belts to rides like Goliath.
If your lap bar ever feels loose don't ride. Tell a worker before the train leaves.
